title: Generative Preset Development — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Generative Preset Development's rich face, its first round at Sketch tier and still a proposal: one made piece, remade once after its challenge, that puts the Profile Concept's perceptual regions to the reader's ear, blind, on the project's own Vital ladders, against the two sets of fences the project has drawn without an ear. I grow when Loudon's ear sets the fences, and I never hold the entry's words.
grain: The page's own ## grain. The Profile Concept is one ## section with its five numbered parts as bold paragraphs, so its piece anchors to the Parameter Vocabulary paragraph and the section is one stamp and one approval.

offers.what: Names only, scoped after the challenge. The page gives four cutoff bands ('closed / dark / open / bright'), three attack regions ('punchy / soft / pad') and four LFO-rate bands ('imperceptible / subtle / obvious / audio-rate'). The project's code holds two vocabularies. Wavetable uses five per family: closed, dark, warm, open, bright; clicky, punchy, natural, soft, swell; imperceptible, drifting, subtle, obvious, fast (ableton-wavetable/corpus_bands.py:24-28, apply_bands.py:46-48 and :51, build_audition_kit.py:199). The Vital generator uses dark, warm, open, bright; punchy, soft, swell; drifting, subtle, obvious (vital/generate_vital.py:35-39). The page's cutoff list has 'closed' and lacks 'warm', so it matches neither. Offer: say the page's lists are examples, or name both vocabularies.

A finding about a method, not about Vital's fences. The rule corpus_bands.py uses for Wavetable, the corpus split into fifths, inherits the synth's defaults; its docstring claims the split puts boundaries 'where designers actually hear a change of character' (corpus_bands.py:13-15). Applied to Vital's corpus as a test of the method: 82 of the 480 presets with filter 1 on sit exactly on cutoff 60, Vital's init, so 'warm' runs 60 to 62.6 st, one rung of the ladder. 242 of 520 sit on the init attack 0.1495 (0.5 ms), so p20 = p40 and 'punchy' has no width. The five cutoff bands are 15.6, 24.4, 2.6, 18.1 and 55.3 st wide and span 0.06, 0.49, 0.10, 0.83 and 2.65 octaves of centroid: even in neither. Leaving out the init-valued presets moves the fifths to 31.6, 50.3, 68.7, 84.8 st (the challenger's count). The Vital generator's own bands are hand-placed and do not fold; nearly even in hertz, they agree with the fifths on 2 of 4 cutoff fences. Wavetable's attack quintiles (0.0001, 0.0010, 0.0015, 0.040 s) look like the same pile at a default, not checked against Wavetable's init. Offer, for the Notes for Future Claude Instances: 'a usage split inherits the synth's defaults; leave out presets sitting on the init value, and at the knob's floor and ceiling, before splitting, or the bands fold onto the blank face.'

verdicts.why: A real blind test with honest loudness matching (BS.1770, 0.04 dB) and right chance (4.0%, 2.1%), but its "project fences" are the Wavetable corpus-fifths rule (corpus_bands.py) applied to Vital; Vital's generator uses hand-placed bands (generate_vital.py:34-41, cutoff rungs 3,5,9,11, agreeing 2 of 4). Remake: name whose fences, add the generator's bands as a scored row, strip the reveal from the caption (it lifts 4/4 to 25% for a reader who knows init is 60), add a bottom-of-ladder arm (attack 2,3,4,5 scores 4/4 unheard), state chance of partly (42.7%, 22.9%), and note the critical-band residual (16.6 phon) in step 2.

remade.what: All five points taken. (1) Two answer keys, named and scored side by side: the Vital generator's bands (cutoff rungs 3, 5, 9, 11; attack 2, 6, 10) and the corpus fifths (3, 5, 6, 9; attack 2, 3, 6). (2) The caption carries no finding; the findings appear only in the reveal. (3) Attack now places the generator's three fences (punchy, soft, swell), not the Wavetable five. A bottom-of-the-ladder arm is added on both knobs. A key that no-listen arms or any guess crowded into the bottom third can fully match is declared refute-only before the trial: the fifths on attack (a crowded-low guess reaches 3 of 3); the generator's key on attack is not reachable (2 of 3 at best). (4) Each rule states the chance of 'partly' (2 to n-1 agreeing): cutoff 51.4% for the generator's key and 38.8% for the fifths; attack 29.4% and 17.1%. The challenger's 42.7% counted 2 or more, so it included full agreement. (5) Step 2 names the 0.04 dB BS.1770 match and the 16.6 phon ISO 532-1 residual, and drops 'only the colour moves'. Not re-challenged.

pieces.title: Where the fences sit · four steps
pieces.caption: **The perceptual regions, put to the ear blind.** Four steps on the project's own renders of Vital's init saw on C3. First the cutoff knob, numbered: semitones, and the hertz they hide. Then the same ladder matched for loudness. Closing the filter alone takes the bottom rung 30.8 dB down; BS.1770 matching brings every rung within 0.04 dB, though a critical-band model still hears the bottom about 16.6 phon quieter. Then a blind placement of four fences, where dark, warm, open and bright begin. Last, three fences on the amp attack: punchy, soft, swell. Each rule states the chance of full and partial agreement before the first rung. Two answer keys stay shut until you have placed your own: the Vital generator's hand-placed bands (generate_vital.py), and the corpus-fifths rule the project uses for Wavetable (corpus_bands.py) applied to Vital's presets. The reveal scores your ear against both and against three placements made without listening, and bakes in each rung's centroid or rise time, recomputed with the project's own code. Measured, not heard: nobody has listened to these renders yet.
